elder sveawolf.herbs: These herbs will not work on your kind in case you are wondering. Take them and you will find her on the hard traveling path that leads from your haunted town. She is near the pointed ears den. Approach her slowly. She is wounded and will strike out at you if she doesn't know your scent. Allow her to smell my scent on you, then feed her the herbs. Make sure she leaves the area. Then return here so we may speak again. Go now and may the goddess light your path.

Dwarven Guard Eske.find her: Now, don't laugh at me when I tell you my story, alright? You see, I am a tough and rough dwarven guard. I've seen my share of trouble, made my share of trouble, and killed more Albions and Hibernians than you can count to! But I have a [pet].
Dwarven Guard Eske.pet: This is no ordinary pet, as we hardly live in an ordinary land! I have a bird, a special bird, one I rescued after a large Hibernian raid on our fair land. We managed to chase off the invaders and while I was helping to tend the wounded, I [saw her].
Dwarven Guard Eske.saw her: She had been struck down by a filthy ranger's bow. Her wing was torn in two, and she was hoping furiously on the ground. She was so sad looking that it touched my stone heart. I scooped her up and made a soft place for her in my [pack].
Dwarven Guard Eske.pack: When I returned to Jordheim and was awaiting my new orders, I nursed her back to health. She stayed with me everywhere I went. She was a beautiful color blue, like the ocean! I called her [Bluebell].
Dwarven Guard Eske.Bluebell: I tried to release Bluebell into the wild many times before my transfer was in order, but she would only look at me confused. She was my favorite thing ever! But when I came to Audliten [disaster] stuck!
Dwarven Guard Eske.disaster: I had let Bluebell out for her morning flying, and she never came back. I fear something dreadful has happened to her, and I am very upset. But I can?t leave my post to search for her. Could you please help me find my [lost Bluebell]?
Dwarven Guard Eske.lost Bluebell: Many thanks to you. To the east of here is where she flew off to. I know there is a nasty smiera-gatto that lurks around there. If she has indeed perished, please return her remains to me.
Dwarven Guard Eske.favor: Trapper Jora had been working on a special ornamental box I could keep Bluebell in when I traveled. I think I will use it now to bury her in. Could you please take this note to Jora and get the box for me? I will be here when you return.

Alomali.bit of a snitch: My master has asked of me [a deed] I cannot complete.
Alomali.a deed: Aye! He asks the impossible! He wishes me to travel to [Striders' Isle] and return to him t he leg of one of [the beasts] there.
Alomali.the beasts: It is the island behind me. A solitary rune stone stands there.
Alomali.willing: Aye, he goes by the name of Lilib. Seek him out and tell him I sent you.

Hurg.a problem: Some nasty minx called Wiley keeps [pestering the town].
Hurg.pestering the town: Yeah! He [won't go away]! He keeps [stealing stuff] from us.
Hurg.stealing stuff: If you get rid of him [I'll] pay ya!

Vik.way to Fort Veldon: Ja! Fort Veldon! On my way from Vasudheim. Bu' me and my men were attacked by [marauding wild animals]!
Vik.marauding wild animals: You'd never believe it if I told ya! Huge creatures they were. [Big jaws I tell ya].
Vik.Big jaws I tell ya: Never seen nothin' like it in my life. Was [the biggest cat] I've seen in my whole life, not to mention it scared off all my men.
Vik.the biggest cat: Oh ya, made a funny sound it sure did, sounded like [hrrrrrgyyf] it did. Had a friend too, mean old Spat!
Vik.hrrrrrgyyf: What's that you say? Oh ya! The blasted beast ran off and took my favorite book, [The Yellow Canary].
Vik.Step #2: Well well, lookie what you brought me! Ye done well and I thannk thee!
Vik.my man Brok: Take this note with ya so ya don't have to explain wha' happened here.
Vik.Spat: I've had some troubles with that nasty friend of Hrrrrgyf's. If you have a minute, I'll [tell you] about that cat Spat and maybe you can give me a hand with him.
Vik.tell you: Always getting into trouble that one is. You'd never believe the [audacity of that cat].
Vik.audacity of that cat: He attacked the wagon with the others and got into a spat, which is why I call him Spat you see, [always been a fighter] that one.
Vik.always been a fighter: Spat picked a fight with that grendalorm, and bit the end of [Vasas tail] right off, just liek that and took off into the hills.
Vik.Vasas tail: Funniest thing I've ever seen I gotta tell ya, but you also gotta know I'd like to [have that tail].

Skorri.driving me crazy: You don't know what's going on, do you? I believe you may be the only one in all of Aegir who hasn't heard the bickering that has been going on between these two. I would have had both of them dragged to Iarnvidur's Lair and left there if Stonelock Stonefist would have allowed it. Instead I have to listen to them [accuse one] another of horrible things!
Skorri.accuse one: Olvaerr here is one of Ota Yrling's Kobolds, who came over with Longbeard and his dwarves. He claims that Ailsa stole something of his. And Ailsa, one of <Player>'s followers claims that Olvaerr stole a totem she was taking to <Player> Gardasdottir, I've been trying to reason with them but they both so stubborn that neither will listen to me when I say that perhaps they simply [lost their belongings].
Skorri.lost their belongings: ENOUGH! Both of you be quiet this instant or I will have you dragged to Delling Crater and thrown in headfirst! Do you see what I have been dealing with? Stonelock, King Goran's brother, put me in charge of leading two groups up into Gripklosa Mountains and unfortunately these two are the leaders of those two groups. neither will budge until they [get back] their missing items and King Goran and Stonelock ill both string me up unless I get them there.
Skorri.get back: <Player>, right? Well <Player>, I was talking to Kaisa and she says she saw both objects before they were lost and knows how to recreate them. Kaisa can't go get the materials because she's been feeling sick lately and I can't leave these two alone for two seconds or they would tear each other apart. If there was someone to [go out and gather] the necessary items.
Skorri.a cloak: Look Olvaerr, this fine <Player> has found your cloak! Please <Player>, give Olvaerr his cloak so that he will no longer think that Ailsa stole it from him. Perhaps he will even apologize to Alisa.
Skorri.gave me something: According to Stonelock, this was made by the finest Troll craftspeople around. I hope you will use it as you explore this land. Perhaps one day we shall speak again and you can join in an expedition I am leading! May the house of Skadi watch over you, <Player>!

Kaisa.lost them: Yes, they lost them. A few days ago Ailsa went out with the totem tied to her belt and didn't come back with it. I'm sure she lost it when she was out studying the Morvaltar for <Player>. As for Olvaerr, Ailsa might be right in hat he lost it in a drinking game [with the dwarves].
Kaisa.with the dwarves: He took a horse to Aegirhamn on the same say that Ailsa went out and he returned the next morning, reeking for ale and groaning about his head. I didn't see the cloak anywhere. It was the same day they both started accusing the other of stealing. I'm just glad I saw both items before they lost them Poor Skorri only has a certain amount of time [to meet Stonelock] up in Gripklosa mountains and if he can't get those two groups moving, Stonelock will be furious.
Kaisa.to meet Stonelock: Stonelock is going to be leading an expedition into the wilds of Gripklosa to track down the truth of yet another rumor about the Troll Fathers. I told Skorri to just go himself and leave both groups here and let <Player> and Longbeard get in trouble for not being able to control their people, but Skorri said Stonelock wouldn't look at it that was. I'd hate for Skorri to [get in trouble] since he's been so kind to check on me while I've been sick.
Kaisa.get in trouble: Well, if we want to keep Skorri out of trouble, we better get you going! Olvaerr's cloak is rather easy to reproduce. From what he was telling anyone who would listen, he killed a mammoth bull himself and sewed it with he sinew from a morvalt bagskytt. But I saw the cloak and know the pelt actually came from a mammoth calf. And I heard Alisa say she saw Olvaerr killing a morvalt ungdom shortly before he started wearing the cloak. I think you can handle getting the pelt and the sinew. Now for [Ailsa's totem].
Kaisa.Ailsa's totem: This will be a bit more difficult. She took the eye of a biting insect and imbued it with the essence of a pyslings. I believe I can reproduce the process she used if you bring me those two things. I know it is a lot to get, but I know that Skorri will reward you well for saving him from those two. Do you [need directions] to the creatures or do you [know the way]?
Kaisa.know the way: Which do you need directions to? the [mammoth] calves, the [morvalt] ungdom, the [pyslings], the biting [insects], or [all of them]?
Kaisa.all of them: The mammoth calves do have a tendency to roam, but you can almost always find some just west of here, in the open area by the rocks. Take care, for the calves usually travel in pairs. Watch out for the young mammoths, they are more than you can handle at this point!

Thorgil.tomte: I'm sorry for the outburst, but these tomtes continue to frustrate me. At one time, the tomtes were actually friendly but now all they do is cause trouble and heartache for the races of Midgard. But you don't want to hear an old man complain about some pests, do you? No one wants to hear about the problem I must now solve because of them. I'm sure you have better things to do. One day I will find someone [willing to listen] to my story and give me a had with my tomte problem.
Thorgil.willing to listen: What? You want to hear my story? I shall be in your debt for just that small favor you grant me now. I am a farmer, or at least I was. I once worked the land not far down the road from here. My house still stands there, but it is infested by those vile creature, the tomtes. But as I said, they weren't always that way. A very long time ago, they [became friendly] with the first settlers that moved into this region.
Thorgil.became friendly: When the first settlers came to this land, the first creatures they encountered were the tomtes. No one had ever seen the strange little men before and were unsure of how they would react to the settlers. The settlers watched the tomtes from afar and observed that they were rather crafty when it came to building things. The settlers, new to the land, knew they would need the help of the tomtes if they were to survive. But the tomtes were unsure of these invaders and they [refused] to have anything to do with the settlers.
Thorgil.refused: It was completely by accident that the tomtes ended up helping the settlers. One of the settlers had left a freshly baked loaf of bread cooling beside the camp fire while she went off into the woods to collect some more firewood. While she was gone, one of the tomtes crept into the camp and tried the strange food. The bread was like nothing he had tasted before and he wanted more. He noticed the water skins of the woman were empty, and he took them and [refilled them].
Thorgil.refilled them: The woman was very surprised when she came back to find here bread gone but here water skins filled. That night, out of curiosity, she left more bread out, along with a broken cooking pan and went to sleep. In the morning she found the bread gone but the pan fixed. She told the other settlers about it, and they did the same thing, with the same results. Leaving bread would result in some chore being done, but no one was sure [who was doing] the chores.
Thorgil.who was doing: The settlers set up a watch and discovered that the tomtes were the ones helping them. The settlers continued to leave bread and other things for the tomtes as they began to farm the land and the tomtes seemed to accept that these few people would be sharing the land with them. They even began to adopt certain farms, including my ancestor's farm. But then more people starting settling in the area, and soon it became [very crowded] for the tomtes.
Thorgil.very crowded: As more people moved in and took up the land, the tomtes were pushed to smaller and smaller areas and the original settlers over time forgot about their little tomte friends. The tomtes grew angry and began to do malicious things to the people living in and around here. Some of us were lucky enough to keep the good favor of the tomtes. My ancestor was one of those people, and up until recently I had tomtes helping myself and my family with our chores but one day that [all changed].
Thorgil.all changed: The tomtes that we had been friendly with suddenly turned vicious, destroying things, hurting my family, tearing up my fields, and hurting the animals I kept. We tried to appease them with bread and other things, but they would take nothing we offered. We stayed as long as we could, but when they attacked my wife and daughter, it was enough. We gathered up everything we could and fled here to Audliten. My wife is currently in Jordheim visiting her sister, and my daughter is off playing somewhere. I remain here to keep an [eye on things].
Thorgil.eye on things: Don't tell my wife this, but when we fled, I left our chest of jewels and money there in the house. I didn't mean to, but we left in such a hurry. I'd go back and get it, but I will not leave my daughter and I cannot take her with me, because the tomtes have overrun the house. I need you to go into the house and get the chest I've hidden there. It's filled with all the treasured things I own. I also need you to do [one other thing] for me.
Thorgil.one other thing: I seem to have lost the key to the chest. As we fled the house, I slipped it into my pocket for safe keeping, but I think it fell out when a tomte grabbed my leg and made me fall. I remember hearing something metal hit the wooden floor of the porch, but I didn't have time to look. The tomte [scavengers] were hurting me, so I just got up and ran for my life. Please, go to my old house and recover my chest of jewels. Once I have it and the key, I will open the box and give you something nice from it. My farm is not far from here. Go east down the road and over the stone bridge. The house lies on the south side of the road. Please, get the key and search the house for the chest. Thank you.
Thorgil.something from you: Would you like something that would add to you [magical power], your [strength], your [dexterity] or your skill with a [sword]? I can only give you one, so think carefully before you make your choice.
Thorgil.sword: Ah, that's a very good choice. I received this bracelet from a woman of great magical power. I know it you will make good use of it. Come back to me soon!
Thorgil.ran into a problem: Hulda's cousins don't live here in Audliten. They are out in the wilds of East Svealand, studying the tomtes. I can't just up and leave here to work with them especially since I just started working with Inga the arrow merchant. I needed a way to support my family, so I spoke with Inga and she agreed to teach me how to make arrows. That's why I'm glad [you've come back] to visit me.
Thorgil.you've come back: I thought perhaps you could go and speak to the brothers and learn about the tomtes. Hulda told me she would let them what has happened to me and what I wanted to know. I was hoping I could [count on you] to give me help with this problem like you did with my lost chest of jewels. If you help me, I'm sure I can find something nice for you in the chest. Well, what do you say?
Thorgil.staff: You cannot use a bow, <Player>. Perhaps a <Player> like you would prefer a nice [staff]?
Thorgil.started to worry: Hulda and Josli helped me ask all of the others in Audliten if they has seen Thorhalla, but no one had seen her since the middle of the day. With one last hope, I headed home, thinking she was hiding somewhere in the house, playing a trick on me. I searched all around but I couldn't find her. All I found was a note written in [a strange language] hidden under the bed.
Thorgil.a strange language: No one around here could read it, but Hulda recognized it. She said that is was tomte writing and that her cousins could read it. I'd go take it to one of them, but I'm afraid to leave the house in case Thorhalla should come back. I would hate to have her find the house empty, since her mother is on her way back from Jordheim. Please, I need your help to [find my daughter]. I feel the tomtes are involved in her disappearance.
Thorgil.chest of jewels: Let's see what I have in here. I have a [bracelet] that adds to your magical power, a [ring] that adds to your general well-being, a [necklace] that adds to your devotion, a [bracer] that will make you quite nimble, and a [mirror] that will show just how attractive you are. Choose carefully!
Thorgil.mirror: Here is your Tomte Skin Bracelet. I got this from old Dielf over there. He said he made it a long time ago from the skin of a tomte shaman. Try it on, I know it will look good on you! Thank you again. Let's hope I won't need your help again, but id I should ever call, I know you will answer!

Bork.looking for something: Hmmm, I may have some work for you. Would you be [interested] in doing a little hunting for me?
Bork.scrolls: Ok here is a tough one. A savage lynx stole a baby from her crib yesterday. Hunt one of these foul creatures down and slay it, then return. Savage lynx are directly West of the Healer hut, go up and over the hill, to a clearing that is surrounded by trees, you should find plenty of them there. [Step #1] Hunt a savage lynx and slay it. [Step #2] Return to Bork Another variant:
Bork.Step #2: Hello again. Are you [interested] in more work already?
Bork.interested: Well let's see here. I think I may have something that you can do for me. Let me check my [scrolls].
Bork.creature: Well here is all I know. It seems to many of the more adventurous sort of the land have called this creature, [Njessi].
Bork.Njessi: I agree that's a very strange name for a monster but I did not choose it. The [reward] for slaying thjis foul beast is quite large. That is good for [many have perished] trying to collect it.
Bork.many have perished: Would you be interested in the [bounty]?
Bork.bounty: The bounty is 70 silver for the head of the [creature]. What do you think?
Bork.this head: I have heard that Raker, the town enchanter, has been looking for one. Perhaps he can do something with it. You should do talk with him.

Gazsi.nonsense: The sea beast, <Player>. There are a few who have expressed interest in having the beast killed and returned to the town, to be displayed as a trophy! Rewards were promised, but still the <Player> it is more valuable to the Musslaklan than it is to the leaders. It would also please me, more, to see the beast everyone around here is calling <Player> give to the Musslaklan. They will use the remains to feed themselves, create items from the bones, and will find some uses for the [carcass], I imagine. They generally do.
Gazsi.carcass: Yes. Kill <Player>, I agree. But don't take the carcass to those expeditionaries who want to display it on their walls or huts as trophies. They will pay you some money, but the musslaklan will pay you in tokens and trinkets. Turn the carcass of <Player> in to a Musslaklan Trader and bring me the trinkets and tokens. The musslaklan know <Player> as Movlor. Remember that. I will pay you a reward for the carcass, and I will pay you for the trinkets. It's your choice.

Hulda.information: I thought so! I figured Thorgil would have to send someone in his place, since I've heard others say that Inga has begun teaching him the art of making and selling arrows. I was very sorry to hear that Thorgil has lost his farm to the tomtes. I was so busy selling shields that I hadn't had a chance to get over and speak with him about what happened. I was glad when he came in here the other day [to ask me] about the tomtes.
Hulda.to ask me: I don't know much, but as Thorgil probably told you, my cousins do. When Thorgil came to me, I couldn't say no to his plea for help. I went and visited each of my brothers and told them of Thorgil's situation. They were both very intrigued by the whole thing, for they have been watching the tomtes around here for many years. Both said they recently observed some changes in [the tomtes' behaviour].
Hulda.the tomtes' behaviour: They both spent a few days watching the tomtes and then trying to make sense of what they saw. I recently received word from both of them, telling me who Thorgil should speak to. But since you are helping Thorgil, I shall tell you [which of my cousins] to speak to.
Hulda.which of my cousins: Both sent me word that they think Edvard would be the best one to help Thorgil. He has noticed some happenings around the tomte camps he watches that his brother Emmerick hasn't noticed. Most people don't know where Edvard likes to hide so I shall tell you. Go across the stone bridge northeast of here to the guard tower. You will find him on the top most level. Take care in climbong the ladders, they can be tricky! Remember to tell him Thorgil sent you!

Edvard Averrson.specific attacks: I believe that the tomtes are trying to find a way to push the people of Audliten and its surrounding area off the lands that once belonged to the tomtes. As more people have moved into the area, the tomtes have been pushed to smaller and smaller areas. There are only a few camps left around here, and because of that ,the residents around here have grown to think the tomtes have moved on or disappeard from this world. But that is [far from the truth]!
Edvard Averrson.far from the truth: The tomtes needed a place that wouldn't be taken over by the residents of the area. They searched and found a cave not far from where my brother watches them. They are crafty little men, and began to carve out a home for themselves under the earth. They worked quickly, and soon their new home was ready. Led by the strongest of the tomtes, <Player>, most of them left their lands and headed deep underground. Now, some people believe that the tomtes in the camps around here don't like dank surroundings of the cave, but that isn ot true. There is [another reason] they live above ground.
Edvard Averrson.another reason: All this time the tomtes have been planning ways to remove the inhabitants of Audliten and the surrounding areas and reclaim them for their own. The tomtes that live in the camps above ground are the eyes and ears for <Player> and report back everything they see. Recently I've noticed more messengers heading down from the north, yet my brother has not noticed and unusual activity around the entrance to the tomte caves. That has led us both to believe [someone else] is behind this plot to drive Thorgil and the others from this area off their land.
Edvard Averrson.someone else: I've noticed many messengers heading in and out of the camp of Edigo. It's my guess that something is going on and he knows about it. I've watched Edigo for some time now and I know he is plotting something. Most likely he's kept the messages that have been sent to him. You must get those messages so we can figure out what is going on and who is sending them. Edigo's camp is not far off from here. Head back through Audliten and take the road east out of town. Go over the stone bridge and keep going until you see the wooden tower. It's not far from Thorgil's old house. You will find Edigo there, but do not go alone! The other tomtes will anwer Edigo's call for help. Return to me when you have any messages. [Step #4] Slay Edigo and obtain any tomte messages. Go through Audliten and head east out of town. Cross the stone bridge and continue to the wooden tower near Thorgil's farm house. (Note: Another possible path for step 4: "Slay Ocug to obtain the tomte messages. To find him, swim across the river beside the guard tower, then head east up the coast to the tomte camp. Do not face Ocug alone!
Edvard Averrson.Step #4: I am impressed. I watched over your battle with the tomtes from here and I liked what I saw. Thorgil did well in selecting you to help him. Now, let's see the messages you obtained.
Edvard Averrson.eager to succeed: A long time ago, Smack displeased <Player> and was forced to leave the tomte caves and live among the races of Midgard. Since then, he has been working to get back into <Player>'s good graces. It seems that he thinks if he can clear the land of invaders, as he sees them, then <Player> will be pleased and restore him to the position he once held. It appears that SMack has recruited Edigo to help in his plot. But now that Edigo is dead, Smack will try to recruit another of the tomtes. You must [stop Smack]!
Edvard Averrson.stop Smack: Gather your forces and lead t hem to Smack's stronghold. You must stop him from contacting any of the other camp leaders. Smack's stronghold isn't hard to find. Take the road east out of Audliten again, and cross the stone bridge. Continue down the road until you see a small stone fort to the southeast. That is where you will find Smack. While you are off dealing with Smack, I shall send word to Thorgil of what you are doing. Return to him when you are finished with Smack.

Aesirdia.able to assist: A thug by the name of [Olag] has been stealing our wares [every night].
Aesirdia.every night: He leaves us stupid notes requesting we deliver him someone by the name of [Wiley].
Aesirdia.Wiley: Yes, we know not exactly when he comes yet we would love to see him [leave for good].
Aesirdia.leave for good: Aye, it is said Wiley is a thief himself. I know nothing more if it.

Emmerick Averrson.are saying: Some of them speak the common tongue we all speak, but most of them speak their own language. My cousin Edvard and I have enchanted different pieces of jewelry that allow the wearer to understand the language of the tomtes. Wear this at all times when you enter the [lair of Nisse]. Once you enter the lair, seek out the handler Nioll. Hopefully he will have some clue that will lead you to Thorhalla.
Emmerick Averrson.lair of Nisse: So you have returned. I'm glad to see you made it out alive. I saw Thorhalla come running out of Nisse's Lair and head back toward Aedliten. Her father will be very pleased that you were able to save the young girl. Now, I wish I could allow you to keep the tomte tooth earring I gave you, but alas, I cannot. Please give it to me now.

Catla Gardasdottir.harness it and use it: The Valkyn do not realize what a gift they have been granted, by being able to call upon the power of the mother. Some of the Valkyn have actually turned away from that power to worship the weak gods of Midgard. I've tried to convince some of them to teach me their ways, but they refuse, providing pathetic excuses? 'It's too dangerous, you'll get hurt, Norse men and women were never meant to wield that power'! How dare they lie to me like that? And [that Kyllikki] is the worst of them!? Catla looks you up and down.
Catla Gardasdottir.that Kyllikki: Kyllikki promised to teach me how to tap into the power of the mother and use the magic granted to the Morvaltar, but she dose nothing but lecture me on the dangers of this spell or that one, and then scribble more things on those scrolls of hers! If I wanted lectures I would have stayed in Jordheim with Gothi of Hel. The time has come for me to do more than just listen! If only I [had her knowledge].
Catla Gardasdottir.had her knowledge: A thought just came to me. I know that Kyllikki will only tell me selected things from the scrolls but never let me actually read them. I really think she just doesn't like me! But she just might give them so someone else. I will reward you well if you were to [obtain the scrolls] for me.
Catla Gardasdottir.getting them out: I know Kyllikki likes to take walks, so when she's out you could search the house. Just don?t let her catch you; get out of the house before she returns! She will be angry over someone trying to steal from her. I wouldn?t ask you to do this but I must have that magic if I am to defeat my enemies! Um, I mean, ah, if Midgard wishes to defeat it's enemies! You will find Kyllikki?s house south of Aegirhamn.
Catla Gardasdottir.once telling someone: She said that each morvalt carries a totem that helps them draw upon the power of the mother. By gathering three of these totems I shall be able to draw upon that power myself. Since you failed to get the scrolls, you must now go and get these totems for me. Morvalt fast-walkers, morvalt spotters, and morvalt jakthasts carry the totems. You must get a totem from each one and return to me. Do not try to use the totems yourself, for you do not know the ritual!!

Kell.terrible upsets: Each evening, as dark appraoches, you can see a clan of what seems to be walking bears [coming from the hills] and laying waste to the area.
Kell.coming from the hills: They [scare and steal] any livestock our past dark as well as many of our goods. We can 't seem to get anyone to trade with us or to stay in the area for long.
Kell.Sydney: Sydney can be found in guard tower up on the hill. You should hurry.

Sydney.about bears: They are clans of bear-men, known as the vendo. They [come from the hills] with little else in mind but terrorizing innocents. Be wary, and keep a good lookout.
Sydney.come from the hills: I have watched as night falls how the hills to the west come alive with motion. Please make haste and be careful. There are many different ones out there, but thou must seek [a specific one].
Sydney.a specific one: Seek out the Vendo Bone-Collectors in the surrounding hills. Bring back to me anything you may be able to obtain from them.
Sydney.translate what it says: I only know of one person who could translate such runes. I, however, don?t know where to [find Virge].
Sydney.find Virge: Please find Virge and have him translate. He is the only one who can help solve this riddle now.
Sydney.Rathis: Rathis must be important. Possible a leader. That should be our target.

Virge.keep this: I shall try and translate these runes the best I can and send you back with it.

Sugnhild.last winter: Last winter was indeed a sad one for me. I lost my [loved one] and also the ring that he gave me in case something might befall him.
Sugnhild.loved one: Gudlor is the town leader, Perhaps you should see him sometime.
Sugnhild.ring: I wish I could have my ring again. [Maybe] you could go and get it for me.

Agnor Crusher.getting ready to attack: Bork says I am seeing things but I think there is a small creature taking notes on us along the river. Maybe you could go and [investigate] for me.
Agnor Crusher.do for you: I knew this day would come. You are taking the book to destroy it? I hope you are strong enough not to give into the temptation that has claimed the others. I have been wearing this cursed ring since Gudlor asked me to [protect it].
Agnor Crusher.protect it: I swear, I think that some of the creatures around here know I have it. The way they look at me makes me very nervous and paranoid. The ring is not even quenched and it still bothers me. I will tell you what I have learned about [the ring].
Agnor Crusher.the ring: To quench the ring you must travel into Uppland, place the ring on your finger and then slay a boreal cockatrice. The ring will only be fed if you are wearing it when the creature dies. Be very careful, the ring will make you feel much weaker while wearing it. Once you have quenched its thirst, return here and I will tell you how to destroy the book. May Odin smile upon you, my friend.
Agnor Crusher.a boulder: The book was actually found there and not in Raumarik. I think that is the best place to try destroying the book. I will know you have failed if the ring appears back on my finger. If the our plan fails, just return the book to Gudlor and we shall try again. I think he was planning on sending you after that cursed crown as well. The ring can only be used to read the book near nidnight. Just stand next to the boulder and wear the ring, then read the spell from the book. Anyway, you should be off. Time is short and you do not want to have both the ring and the book on you any longer than you have to. Trust me, bad things may happen to you if you delay too long.

Aylarn.protector: I have heard rumors of an evil creature that wears a magical cloak. Perhaps you would like me to [share the tale] I heard.
Aylarn.few nights: A young dwarf came stumbling out of the brush and cried for hours. He said he was the son of Arik of Haggerfel. He said he was only 14 winters old and had become [lost].
Aylarn.lost: He said a strange robed creature that called herself Ulga, had led him into the forest in promise of adventure and [cast some magic] on him. He said he wandered the forest for the last two nights.
Aylarn.cast some magic: I did not have the heart to explain to him what had happened. If there is a creature stealing life wandering about the forest, then someone should put an end to that. Don't you think?

Rollo.can't rest: Surely, the smith told you? My story is one [passed down] the line of dwarven smiths. The story of how I, Rollo, failed my master, <Player>.
Rollo.passed down: Aye, it is passed down. <Player> left me to care for items he had forged or helped create for use by all Dwarves. I failed! Ugnof and his men heard of this changeable item and [stole it].
Rollo.stole it: Aye, stole it. Killed me. For 300 years, the spawn of Ugnof have been carrying the <Player> item. For 300 years I have wandered these hills cursing his name! I shall not rest until someone can [retrieve the <Player> item].
Rollo.retrieve the <Player> item: Aye, fare well, then, seek out Ugnof Toestubber in the lands named Western Svealand (You will find Ugnof walking outside the perimeter of Hugginfel with a Blodfeleg [Thralldriver] and a Blodfeleg Warhound, both will join in the fight.) Return with <Player> to Hilde, in Haggerfel, and my soul shall rest!

Gudlor.Thegn Aki: It is said he wears a special helm, crafted for his sire, the great [General Aki]. I am sure it is magical however I am not quite sure its purpose.
Gudlor.General Aki: General Aki was said to be a great leader among men. Unfortunately, he only allowed men in his ranks. He was a friend of [Konung], Botolf's father. General Aki was reumored to be able to use magic as well, only his dead enemies knew just how much though.
Gudlor.Konung: Go gather your forces and quit wasting time! There will be time to worry about Redhands later. May the gods have mercy on us if you fail.
Gudlor.Blodfelag: I have been told that he was captured and his tongue removed. Redhands had one of his Runemasters cast a mind control rune on Fridgeir, turning him into nothing more than a [guard dog]. Now he serves as a warning to any who would dare cross Redhands.
Gudlor.guard dog: I think naught can be done for this Frdgeir and have not told Sugnhild of his plight. Perhaps one day someone will tell her but that is not today. Someone should also [go to the Blodfelag keep] and put Fridgeir out of his misery.
Gudlor.go to the Blodfelag keep: What? You think you could? Well all I know about the location of the keep is that it is very far down the road. You will have to get past many dangers to [acutally] reach it.
Gudlor.well: Sadly, we have had our share of problems here in Huginfell. The Svartalf raids continue daily but we have managed to survive. There has been [something] else that has been plaguing my mind, but before I tell you what it is, I must tell you another older story. Do you have some time to listen?
Gudlor.few followers: Redhands began gathering more followers and set about his plans to take over the local ruffians. It is told that he sent his men into the far reaches of Raumarik seeking something to give him enough power to take complete control of the area. His men returned with an ancient [tome of runes].
Gudlor.tome of runes: The tome was said to have some of the most powerful runes in existence. They were called the runes of creation, which were used in the formation of Midgard itself. Unfortunately, most of the runes in the book were beyond the understanding of mere [mortal] men.
Gudlor.mortal: Redhands called upon Lord Loki to aid him in his quest and a child came to him, bearing a dark ring. The child told Redhands the rind was cursed and somehow gave its bearer the power to read the tome. Redhands called upon his most trusted Runemaster and had her [wear the ring].
Gudlor.wear the ring: She screamed and fell to the ground as a rotting corpse. Next, Redhands called on his second most trsuted Runemaster and ordered hiim to wear the ring. He slipped the ring on and began to decipher some of the tome, learning its [dark secrets].
Gudlor.dark secrets: The first ones he learned about were the rune of power and the rune of damnation. The Runemaster attempted to craft a crown with the rune on it, but could not master the skills needed. He did, however, create a crown that made its bearer extremely strong and qucik but slowly drove them [insane].
Gudlor.insane: Redhands knew a good use for such a cursed item. He gave the crown to the leader of the Blodfelag as a gift. The Blodfelag Commander wore the crown and was slowly [driven mad].
Gudlor.driven mad: The Commander's men could no longer trust him to make good decisions and Redhands was more than willing to take control in his place. Redhands ordered the Commander to give up his crown or die. The Commander was not willing to give up his cherished crown and was last seen heading into Muspelheim, vowing to [never surrender] his crown to anyone.
Gudlor.never surrender: He is probably still there with that cursed crown on his head. Next, Redhands turned [his attention] to us.
Gudlor.his attention: He had his Runemasters carve Runes of Damnation around the town to summon and control legions of dead to attack us. If not for Sugnhild's brave husband, Fridgier Gestsson, we would have been [surprised] and the town lost.
Gudlor.surprised: Fridgeir managed to alert his wife just as the last symbol was carved and we hunted the Runemasters, slaying them. The shadows rose from the mists and started slaying who stood against them. That was the longest [night]of my life.
Gudlor.night: The battle lasted until dawn when the shadows were driven away by the morning light. I went searching for survivors and only [found this].
Gudlor.found this: I honestly do not know if this book can be destroyed. I pray to Odin every night, hoping that someone will be able to take [the book] from me without taking my life. Only time will tell though.
Gudlor.the book: Now you need the rinf that came with the book. I gave it to Agnor Crusher so I would not be tempted to use the book. He hates protecting the ring but I can trust no other with it. You can find him guarding the northern part of the town from the Blodfelag. Thank you, my friend, for undertaking this dangerous quest.
Gudlor.evil crown: Someone must go and get the crown back so innocents are not controlled by its twisted powers. I think that person is you. You should be able to get where the crown is with little danger because of your strong will. In any case, it will be safer with you. Legends say the Blodfelag king, Strykel, went deep into Muspelheim to hide. I do not believe he made it very far before he was completely [taken over] by the crown.
Gudlor.taken over: It changed him into a demonic monster and he is said to roam a fiery island just east of the Muspelheim gate. By Odin's will, you should be able to find Strykel and release his spirit to the gods. It shall be left to you how to guard the crown. Perhaps we shall try to destroy this book again another day. Until then, I shall guard it with [my life].
Gudlor.my life: Go now and one warning. If you are slain while wearing the crown, it may have the power to animate your corpse and slay your friends. Be forewarned, the crown is truly twisted evil. Safe journey to you, my friend.

Saydyn.visions: I have seen visions of a vile creature that has turned against the gods themselves. I could only watch, helpless, as it captured lone travelers and changed them into the [walking dead].
Saydyn.walking dead: If he is not stopped, he will gather an army of dead and begin launching attacks on the cities of our fair lands. Lady Eir has called upon you to help us. Will you [answer her call]?
Saydyn.find the creature: The foul stench of the creature is enough to almost guide you there but you may find it by heading down the road and walking on the ridge across from the Svartalf village. May Thor himself smile on your journey.

Sentry Dwarn.tale: Wonderful, let me tell you of [<Player>], the pious Saracen.
Sentry Dwarn.<Player>: Aye, <Player>, never a more pious woman was to be had here in Midgard. She was a slave here, brought back from a raid on a settlement in northern Albion. She never complained about her plight, but she continuously [prayed].
Sentry Dwarn.prayed: She prayed several times a day to her God. When the fever struck her, she prayed even harder, asking him to [preserve her piety]. He granted her wish.
Sentry Dwarn.preserve her piety: It was said that her God took part of her soul and imbued it within a [tunic] she had been making.
Sentry Dwarn.tunic: This tunic, once given her spirit, danced away, out into the forest and was never seen again. I, for one, believe that no such thing happened, but if you're up for some [adventure], I can tell you where most think it is.

Atzar.to leave me alone: I have a friend, Dunfjall, who is an expert at getting people to like him. He used to be a skald and he knows how to charm people. Well, he's spent some time studyingf the arachites, werewolves, and svartalfs and knows all their little secrets. He helped me with my werewolf problem. You know , he could probably [give you a hand] with one of those groups, if you're interested. The thing is, you can only improve your status with one group.
Atzar.give you a hand: It would take a little work on your part, but if you're [up to the challenge], I'm sure that Dunfjall would help you. What do you say?
Atzar.had his belongings: There was a disagreement between the rwo werewolves, and the one left, taking some of the others with him. They came here to Myrkwood and settled into the forest, not far from here. At first, the residents if the town, <Player>, did not know of their presence. Understand that back then, the werewolves had a human form during the day. It has only been over time that they changed and assumed the form the have today. I do not know the entire story, but I know that something bad happened and it resulted in the werewolves taking over [<Player>].
Atzar.<Player>: The werewolves that live there now raise their young and let them tear up the land and terrorize the people. It was those pups that attacked me and stole Trustan's favorite sword. I know Trustan would want it back, and I'd go and get it from him, but have some other things of his to find. Trustan loaned a few of this things to another friend and I must get those things back before I can send everything up to him. Please, seek out the werewolf pups that scamper behind Gna Faste and get back Trustan's sword. Please!
Atzar.the arachites: The arachites are another group that like to cause trouble around here, but Curka can tell you more about them. Here, take this and grab a horse to Galplen. It's not far, but it can be dangerous getting there. Seek out Curka and tell her Atzar sent you for the shield. Once you have it come back to me, and then we'll send you up to Trustan!
Atzar.to recover: I'm sure Curka talked about the svartlafs when you were with her. She always talks about them and how bad they get treated. Well, I can see why they get treated that way after what they did to me! While you were away, I wanted to get a peek at what the werewolves were up to. Living so close to <Player>, it's natural to want to know what's going on. While I was out in the forest I got attacked by the svartalfs! They seemed to think I [support the werewolves].
Atzar.support the werewolves: I know where these svartalfs who attacked me like to hide. Take the road south from here until you get to the rock that directs you to Galplen. Then you need to go east into the woods. They hide way back in the woods, so be careful! Just south of there you will find a full camp of the svartalfs! If they don't like you, and they may not after you get that helm back, they will attack. Oh, before you go, give me that shield so I can pack it up.

Dunfjall.a problem: That happens a lot around here. People get into trouble with the svartalfs and they can't get out of it without some help. I'm that help. I know all their secrets, plus those of the arachites and werewolves. Unfortunately, if I'm popular with one group, the other two groups usually hate me until I do something for them. Then the first group hates me again. It's a never-ending cycle. One day I'll figure out how to get in good with all three groups, but until then, I'll take them one at a time. Now, it's [decision time] for you.
Dunfjall.decision time: Like I said, I don't know how to become friendly with all three groups. What you do may not make you friendly, but it will help you get close to that goal. I will also warn you now, sometimes you may need a partner to help you do the things I ask. So now, you must choose which group you want to improve your standings with. Will it be the [werewolves], the [svartalfs], or the [arachites]? Choose wisely for you may not change your mind, nor may you work with me again. I cannot reveal all my secrets to you or I would lose my place with all three groups! Now, choose.

Gord.not: Now these are very powerful staffs. You will be expected to uphold the traditions of all the Spiritmasters that have come before you. I will give you one of the staffs that I have already prepared. That way you din't have to wait.

Trustan.all the fighting: You haven't heard about Myrkwood? Well then listen up, friend! You must be wary of the three big groups that live there. There are the svartalfs, the arachites, and the werewolves. Each group cannot stand the others, and they have made life miserable for the folks that live in Myrkwood. They fight with each other and sometimes with us! I had enought of it and just moved here to Huginfell. I hope life here in West Svealand will be better. I just wish I had remembered to bring all [my belongings].
Trustan.my belongings: I had to leave some of my things in Gna Faste. I paid for a horse to bring me here, and since I'm not a little person, the horse couldn't carry both me and all my things. I had some friends of mine in Gna Faste hold on to the rest of the things. I would go back there and get them myslef except while I was riding up here, I kind of [fell off the horse].
Trustan.fell off the horse: I had never ridden a horse before my trip up here, and I was unsure of myself, and the horse could sense my nrevousness. I guess I should have just walked but Atzar said I'd be okay. I was almost there when something spooked the horse and it threw me to the ground. I landed on my arm and it broke. I can't ride horses until it heals, but I'd like my things. Say, you seem kind. You've listened to me tale to this point. Do you think you would help me out and [get my things] from Atzar for me? I will repay you for your kindness.

Curka.be a problem: I don't have the shield, the arachites do. Atzar must have mentioned the arachites. They are these spidery type people that live in Myrkwood. Worst thing that ever happened to Myrkwood were those arachites. They didn't start off the way they are, you know. A very long time ago they were spiders. But Myrkwood is a dark forest, and sometimes strange things happen. The power of Myrkwood [affected those spiders].
Curka.affected those spiders: I had taken Trustan's shield over to Nalliten to show it to a friend of mine who wants to make his own shield. I went there and spent a few days helping my friend make his shield. It was on my way back that I ran into trouble. A group of arachite younglings ran out of the forest and attacked me. They screamed at me, saying those that helped the svartalfs would die. Apparently they could sense my friendship with them. I had to run or else I would have been killed. I threw Trustan's shield at them and ran for the guard tower. They picked up the shield and ran the other way. Now I fear the shield is [lost forever]
Curka.lost forever: You know, you look strong enough to handle those arachite younglings. I am not brave or strong, which is why I ran for the guards at the first sight of trouble. Please, go find these younglings and kill them for me. It is the only way to retrieve Trustan's shield, and it will set you on the raod towards building a good relationship with the svartalfs. Head out through the northeast gate and follow the road. When you reach a split in the road, keep going straight to the guard tower. At the tower, head southwest into the woods. You will find the younglings there. Return to me when you have the shield.
Curka.Atzar: Here take this ticket to Gna Faste. The horses are so much faster than walking! I shall send word to Trustan that you retrieved his shield so he can make you a nice present for your work. He's quite the craftsman! Now, hurry along to Gna Faste!

Halla.sturdy sort: Yes, sturdy sort. You look to Halla like a smart, strong, warrior! Maybe Halla has a [story] for you.
Halla.story: Halla's story is scary! Maybe you should close your ears? Ha ha! No, Halla's just joking. Have you ever heard of the bear the locals call [Stripe]?
Halla.Stripe: Good, then Halla will make sure you hear about nasty old Stripe. Long ago, there was a man named Varnarn who loved Hel and [served her] for most of his life.
Halla.served her: Varnarn was a Spiritmaster for a long time, long long time, and Hel was going to reward him for his service, when he tried to [trick] Hel and take over the Underworld!
Halla.trick: Yes, But little did he know Hel turned his own trick on him, foiling his ploy and angering her at the same time. As his punishment, he was turned into a [bear].
Halla.bear: A bear the locals call Stripe. Halla doesn't know why he's called Stripe, but Halla hears tell of a [magical item] Stripe carries with him.

Thrand.working for them: Yes, working for them. But my brother isn't anything like that. He's great at hiding in the shadows and maybe he's redistributed a little wealth, but I don't think that he'd work for the Svartalfs. He is a good person, not a killer! I just know something is wrong. He won't tell me anything though, he thinks he's protecting me. But he might talk to you. Do you think you could go [see him] for me?
Thrand.trust: Ah you're right. Piercer won't trust you either. Hmmm, let's see, I know! Tell him you have a message for Halvor. That's his real name and if you use it he'll know I sent you. Good luck, I just hope it's not too late. He's the only family I have.

Piercer.kill someone: Shhhh! Not so loud. Yes, murder. You're probably not familiar with the Svartalfar, so before I ask you to help me I'll explain a little about them. The Svartalfar, the Arachites and the Varulv are all involved in a long-standing dispute over the Myrkwood area. The Svartalfar think that they were there first and that the other two groups are invading their [territory].
Piercer.territory: The three factions are constantly fighting amongst themselves, sometimes in open combat, but more often they send agents to murder key personalities and sabotage plans. The Svartalfar have become adept at sneak attacks and assassinations and are pretty unscrupulous about what they'll agree to do to increase their holdings and resources. I didn't realize they were such a bad bunch when I first got involved and now they won't let me leave. They say they're going to kill my brother Thrand if I don't do this job for them! Can you [help] me?
Piercer.help: Maybe Graesen will talk to you. I report to him, and if you tell him that I'd be a terrible assassin maybe he'll just let me leave. See the camp below? Graesen is just to the east of it.
Piercer.returned: A Svartalfar named Rip was told to do the job. He's big, mean, and won't stop until he's done it. I think the best thing would be for you to take the initiative and go after him first. He is Southwest of here, under a tree outside the main camp.

Graesen.Piercer: He's a new guy, and a pitiful fool that don't have no guts. Promised he'd do a job, now says he's scared.
Graesen.do it: The agent is in Myrkwood, disguised as an arachite priest (or weblasher or shadowslinker for another version). Just tell him Graesen sent you.

Sinna Redtoes.no more maps: Hrmph, no more maps in there and that's lucky for you! Someone crept in here while I was sleeping and stole two maps that belong to Longbeard. He put them in my care until he our forces came back from helping Stonelock fight the Morvltar. They are due back any day and the maps I had the Valkyn draw me are gone. I think I know [who did it] but I'm not completely sure.
Sinna Redtoes.who did it: I caught a glimpse of their clothes as they ran our with the maps. I believe they were members of the Grenlock Clan. I would go talk to the Grenlock Clan about it but I must try to recreate both those maps. The Valkyn who drew them went out with Stonelock and won't return until the rest of our group comes back. I need someone who will [track down these thieves] and retrieve my maps.
Sinna Redtoes.Step #15: I have a Fiery Garnet [belt], a Spirited Amber [necklace], a Luminous Citrine [pin], a Terrence Adventureine [choker], a Chilly Sodalite [earring], and a Potent Amethyst [gem]. I can tell you about each one if you wish, of you may [choose now].
Sinna Redtoes.choose now: The Firey Garnet belt was made by my grandfather and will aid in resisting fire as well as add to you strength and dexterity. Would you like the [Fiery Garnet] belt or would you like to hear [about the others]?
Sinna Redtoes.about the others: The Spirited Amber necklace is very nice. Wearing it will make you dexterous and quick, as well as help you resist those that attack your mind. Do you choose the [Spirited Amber] necklace or would you like to hear [about the others]?
Sinna Redtoes.Potent Amethyst: Here is your Potent Amethyst gem. I shall sing your praises tonight as I raise a horn of ale with Longbeard. May the House of Eir always watch over you.

Keirstyn Alfevson.she is correct: A few days ago I awoke to find that four members of the Clan had disappeared. At first I figured that my brother Karle had sent them into the wild lands, since their packs were gone. When I heard later that day that Sinna Redtoes had seen Grenlock Clan members around her packs, I began to wonder. I went to Karle and he denied sending the four on any kind of mission. It was then that I [remembered something].
Keirstyn Alfevson.remembered something: That evening at dinner, before the four disappeared, I heard one of the men, Modolf, mention the town of Knarr in Munin Sound. I think I heard one of the missing women mention the word 'treasure' but I cannot be sure. Ever since I learned of the theft, I have been trying to track down the four without luck. I know Sinna sent you here to get the maps back. I cannot give you maps I do not have, but I can give you this. Use it to get to Knarr quickly and ask around the town to see if anyone has seen or heard of Modolf. I wish you luck.

Heikki.my little boat: As he got into the boat I wondered if I had done the right thing selling him the boat. He had no clue what he was doing. Can you believe a Norseman who doesn't know how to handle a boat? I showed him how to row it properly and then he headed out northeast across the water and followed the coastline until I lost sight of him. I figured that was the last I'd see of him or my little boat but [I was wrong].
Heikki.I was wrong: I wasn't on watch the next night, so I decided to do a little hunting before sunset. I went up the coast past the Shalklan camp and what did I find on shore? Modolf's pack, soaked with water and my little boat, upside down, with a big hole in it! I know I had sold the boat, but I was still upset. I began to drag the boat back to here when I realized that I hadn't seen Modolf anywhere, just his pack. I went back and search for him but I couldn?t find him anywhere. But that time the sun had set and that is [not a good time] to be far from home.
Heikki.not a good time: Many people have drowned out in that part of the land. I think the mist menaces that roam around there confuse people and they end up capsizing their boats. At night the spirits of those drowning victims come out and haunt the land. If Modolf did drown, that's where you'll find his spirit. That's all the help I can give you. I wish you luck in finding him.

Merja.pay the price: Then you must find Loden and Idette. I would go seek them myself, but I still have a shred of hope that they will return here. If they do I will get the maps from them and hold them until your return. The people here say they saw Loden and Idette heading kind of east from here, through a valley and then they turned north. How far they got, I don't know, but that's where you should start searching. I'm sure they won't give up the map halves easily, so be careful. You may even want to take some friends with you. Come back to me when you have both halves and I will reassemble the map for you.

Dalla.adventure: I sought glory, treasure, and companionship, much like I'm sure you do. I found it, and a whole lot more. Adventuring had its ups and [downs] for me.
Dalla.downs: Aye. My group and I were traveling through Skona Ravine, a most dangerous area, dodging the werewolves that live there, when we ran into a [large cat].
Dalla.large cat: This cat hissed at us and lunged at one of my group mates. He slashed at him pretty good, all the while making a [furf noise]. With the help of our skald, we outran the thing.
Dalla.furf noise: Yes, A strange noise indeed. Over the next few hours, we spoke of the cat often, but [didn't dare return].

Darrius.stay home: I have even had to sell some of my most treasured objects to gather money so I will be able to support my family. I am almost saddened that I may never get to journey back to Galplen in search of the crown I [read] about.
Darrius.read: Aye, I had this old book and I had managed to translate some of it. It told a story about werewolves and how they came from a far away land to our shores and settled down in the fort of Askheim, in Myrkwood. It also mentioned the leader of the werewolves, a Baron Falwar, has a mystical crown. The crown has been passed down from werewolf leader to leader. At least I managed to earn a few coin from the sale of the book. I [sold it] to two trolls.
Darrius.sold it: It is an [interesting] story. Would you like to hear more about the tale of two trolls?
Darrius.rolled around: I told them to get out. I was amazed that they wanted their money back because the book was torn up. They are probably somewhere in Gaplen trying to sell someone what is left of the book. I am kind of [glad] I sold the book.
Darrius.glad: A few days after the trolls bought the book, a strange woman came through town searching for it. She said that an old Runemaster had told her I had it. She seemed really upset when I told her I sold the book and wanted to know [who] bought it.
Darrius.who: I told her that the troll called himself Aki and had said he was returning to Galplen. The woman said she studied werewolves and wanted any knowledge the book contained. I told her I didn't know anything else.
Darrius.werewolves: They are cursed. Legend tells of people who could change into forest creatures but only because of their faith. The werewolves can change others into werewolves with but a single cite. That is why I did not mind trying to [steal from them].
Darrius.steal from them: The crown sounds like it could be a worthy prize for someone strong enough to go get it. If I were you, I would go to the stables and get a horse. You can reach Galplen much faster if you ride. Aki should be selling his wares somewhere around town. Talk to him about it.

Arnleif.Krrrck: Ah such a sad tale. Originally, Krrrck was a priest of <Player>, helping oyung Hunters learn the ways of the woods, as well as tutoring villagers on how to survive the harsh winters. His name was [Erik].
Arnleif.Erik: Erik was very improtant to <Player>, and she rewarded him well for his services. Loki, ever the mischief-maker, decided to trick <Player> and turned her friendly priest into a [frog].
Arnleif.frog: A large troll indeed! When the Goddess came to find Erik, all she found in his temple was this large frog. Not knowing what had happened to Erik, <Player> went in [search] of him.
Arnleif.search: She searched high and low for him, coming back to his temple twice a day to see if he had returned. The only one waiting for her was the [miserable], lonely frog.
Arnleif.miserable: <Player>, still unhappy with the disappearance of her priest, took the frog to [Skona Ravine] where he could be with other wildlife.
Arnleif.Skona Ravine: Skona Ravine and a wonderous place, filled with many creatures and various healing plants. It is said that Erik wishes to be released from his [imprisonment] and rejoined with his goddess, <Player>.

Juuso.that crazy woman: I think you know whom I speak on! None other than Catla! You must have realized that she is very unstable. If she continues with her plan it won't be long for her to be completely insane. I'm sure she has told you she wants to tap into the power of the mother of the Morvaltar. She refused to accept the fact that humans cannot wield that power! You know she has been asking ever Valkyn in Aegir's Landing to help her out, right? There was [only one] who was brave enough to take on working with Catla.
Juuso.only one: I'm sure Catla mentioned Kyllikki to you. Anyone who has talked with Catla has heard of Kyllikki and how she has refused to teach Catla anything else. You are not the only one who was asked to get those scrolls. Catla wanted them more than anything and she asked everyone she ran into to get them. I know you helped her because she came to me and [ordered me] to help her when the scrolls didn't give the information she wanted.
Juuso.ordered me: Yes, she ordered me to help her! She said she heard that I knew of a potion that would let her use the power of the mother and I was to make it for her so that she could use that power. It is true that I have learned some ways to draw upon that power, but most of my strength come from Bogdar and the potion is very dangerous. I tried to tell her that but she would hear none of it! All she wants to hear is that she can use the power of the mother to [destroy her enemies].
Juuso.destroy her enemies: She longs to destroy Albion and Hibernia for what happened to her family and I swear she'll destroy anyone who gets in her way of doing that. I've even heard her make remarks about taking control of Midgard! She scares me! She threatened to have my spirit sucked into the depths of Hel's domain if I didn?t do as she ordered. What was I to do? I must make the potion but I must also go to Catla and tell her everything I know about Morvaltar. She doesn't understand I can't do both at once and that I [need someone] to collect the ingredients for the potion.
Juuso.need someone: Thank you! You may have save both of our lives if you are able to get the things that we need for the potion. It will not be an easy task, but I have many friends that will help me reward you well for this. And it is to [one of these friends] that you must go first.
Juuso.one of these friends: Before I came here to Aegir's Landing I spent some time with the Skalklan in Munin Sound. An oyster-gathering Skalklan named Edrigu taught me many secrets of the Skalklan. One of those secrets was the potion Catla spoke of. Edrigu had enough purpose for it, but it had an interesting side effect on many. It allowed the drinker to speak directly to the spirit of the mother, who would then grant more of her power to use. One of the ingredients can [only be obtained] from Edrigu.
Juuso.only be obtained: That is a problem for you. The Skalklan are not very welcoming to outsiders and will not talk to you if you approached them. But fear not! Edrigu and the other Skalklan know me and will speak to one who carries a sign from me. I have an amulet that Edrigu would recognize but it's missing [one piece].
Juuso.one piece: The Skalklan do not like the creatures called [ingesters] that live in Munin Sound. Getting a wiggly tentacle from one would help prove that you want to be a friend to the Skalklan. Once you get a wiggly tentacle, you will need to set it in the middle of this amulet. The Skalklan will leave you alone as long as you wear it, but if you should harm a single Skalklan while you wear it, it will destroy the amulet and they could possibly hate you! Seek out Edrigu and tell him Juuso sent you. He will know what I seek. I wish you luck!
Juuso.three creatures: First you must find a woolly mammoth and obtain some of its fur. The fur will tether Catla in this world so that she will not become lost in the spirit world while she searches for the mother. After you have the fur, you will need the blood of [two Morvaltar].
Juuso.two Morvaltar: Take these vials and return them filled with the blood of the Morvalt vandarare and the Morvalt streber. Their blood, when mixed with the fluid from Edrigu and the fur, is what allows the communication with the mother. It will not work for Catla but she must learn that for herself. She will not listen to reason! Once you have filled both vials return to me so that I may complete the potion and save us both from Catla's wrath!
Juuso.what you want: My friends have given me [swords], [hammers], [axes], [staves], a [spear], a [bow], and axe for your [left hand] and [hand to hand], weapons. Which would you prefer? Once you choose you cannot change your mind!
Juuso.hand to hand: Would you like a [one-handed] or a [two-handed] hammer?
Juuso.two-handed: Here is your Beinbrottsjo war hammer. I hope it will help to defend you against Catla if she should ever completely lose her grip on sanity. I must go to her now and deliver this potion that will not work for her. Wish me luck!

Topi.do some good: I know, I know? Everyone wants to get something out of everything. Greedy bastards and sons of? well, nevermind that. Anyhow, I'll make sure it's worth your time. Now here's what I need you [to do].
Topi.to do: Well, yeah, of course you'll have to work for it. Nothing's free, you know. hehe Anyhow, there are they morvalt strebers around here that have been causing some [problems] with the locals.
Topi.problems: If you can defeat one in battle and bring me it's scalp, I'll reward you for it. But be warned. They are nasty creatures and will eat you up if you aren't ready for the [challenge]. Good luck.

Maerta.assistance: I am in short supply of my [ice water]. I use it while making my asterite bars.
Maerta.ice water: I know, everyone else things I'm a bit dense. I can't just use any ice water. I must use the ice water from a snow giant. It has a magical [property] that allows me to craft my bars in half the normal time. If someone were able to slay a few of these snow giants and gather its water in a vial I could get back on track.

Nyvad.Tyr: Oh, so you think I'm lying, is that it? Well, I can tell you I most certainly am not! I am a mighty thane! Nyvad the Great! Perhaps you have heard of me, yes? Well, no matter, I am here to [right the wrongs].
Nyvad.right the wrongs: Oh yes, I'm here to help get rid of the cultist threat! You see, they are very bad people, very bad. I'm here to help, well, eliminate the threat! Yes, but you see, I am rather erm? busy, fighting off [other threats].
Nyvad.other threats: I don't have time to devote to strictly the cultists. There is other evil afoot here in Munin Sound. Tricky enemies sneak up always! We are constantly alert! Say, we could use someone like you. Why not [join the fray] and help all of Munin Sound?!
Nyvad.join the fray: Excellent! I knew you'd be a great [candidate] for this job. It's simple, really. All you have to do is return some cultist staves to me and I will reward you richly! Yes, that I sill. Now, be off, friend of Munin Sound! Return to me safely!

Birgir.sioalf cultists: Yeah! They've been coming around here and stealing my stuff! It's hard for a man to make a profit if people are always snatching your things and not paying for them! I've got four hungry mouths to feed, you know? Oh, how I'd like to get back at those cultists... Say... are you looking for a [job]?
Birgir.job: Great! Look, all you have to do is get my supplies back for me. They took a bunch, so I'm sure you'll have to go back to their camps a few times to get it all. I'll be sure to reward you somehow. Thanks a lot friend, and [remember], be careful!

Anakoll.assistance: Yes. There have been some undead around here lately that are causing problems. Specifically, the [yellowed skeletons].
Anakoll.yellowed skeletons: I have been studying them for some time now, but I have yet to be able to get my hands on a sample of their bones. If you can, please get me some bones so I might be able to complete my [research].

Torlieva.Listen: Woolly Mammoths give our hunters hard time. But mammoths good eating and clothing. YOu go out and get mammoth hides for us. Harsh winter is coming. Need [warm] clothes.
Torlieva.warm: Yes. We fish, get food that way, but clothes very [important]. Go now. Come back when you have hides!

Jolgeir.assistance: I'm running low on lifebane, but don't have time to gather one of the components I need to make a new batch. The lifebane has to be kept extremely cold, so I use the cold blood of frost giants. I can't pay you, but if you would get some for me, I'm sure it would be a good [experience] for you. Frost giants put up quite a fight, and you can hone your skills against them. I suggest you seek them in Yggdra Forest.

Frakki.information: Excelent! There's a lot of talk going around that the local magistrate is going to start cracking down on the [redcap skulkers].
Frakki.redcap skulkers: The little buggers are everywhere it seems, always getting into our supplies. grrr... Anyhow, if you come across any, bring their [red caps] back to me and I'll pass them on to the authorities.
Frakki.red caps: Ok, listen, they are easy to get, just off one of the little buggers and bring me the cap. Now be off. Time's [wasting]!

Rith.Listen: Thir in charge of making rope and nets for tribe. Fishing easy for us, but best rope come from the Cave Lioness [sinew].
Rith.sinew: Cave Lioness fierce hunters. Very protective of territory. Kill many [musslaklan] warriors. But you stronger than us. Go now, get us some sinew so we can have stronger nets and rope.
